Mary (on the LEFT) leans towards Jesus (on the RIGHT) at a low table and tells him quietly that the wine has run out; her face is concerned, one open hand towards a small empty clay jug and two cups on the table. Jesus turns his face to her, calm and attentive. The wedding is only hinted at by one pale wash and two or three faint figures in the far background. Medium shot. Even in this reduced style Mary must clearly look like the mother of a grown man: grey-white hair visible at her forehead under the veil, a few clear lines on her face and around her mouth, slightly stooped shoulders – she looks clearly older than Jesus, about the age of a grandmother.

PEOPLE AND OBJECTS (keep exactly):
- Mary, the mother of Jesus: clearly one generation older than her adult son, grey streaks in her dark hair visible under the veil, gentle lines around eyes and mouth, slightly stooped posture; blue-grey veil and blue-grey robe.
- Jesus: a Galilean man in his early thirties, shoulder-length dark brown wavy hair, short full dark beard, warm brown eyes, olive skin, a kind and open face that is always fully visible like everyone else's; cream linen tunic and a muted terracotta-red mantle over one shoulder. No halo. He is the only person wearing terracotta-red.
- A small empty clay wine jug.

WHO SPEAKS:
- Mary, the mother of Jesus is speaking to jesus (shown through gaze and gesture).
- Jesus is speaking to mary, the mother of jesus (shown through gaze and gesture).

PICTURE: Landscape picture, a single scene (not a comic page, no panel borders, no frame). No lettering of any kind and no speech bubbles. Keep the upper third of the picture as empty white paper, because speech bubbles are added there later. Use as few people and objects as the scene needs. Every person and every important object stands completely inside the picture with empty paper on every side; nobody is cut off by an edge; the washes fade out into the white paper towards the edges.

STYLE: Very reduced, loose watercolour sketch for adults, like a quick painted study in a sketchbook – much simpler than a finished book illustration. Most of the sheet is untouched warm white paper. Only a few thin, broken ink lines that suggest forms instead of outlining them; many contours are left open or missing. Colour as a few flat, transparent, pale washes that bleed softly and do not fill the shapes completely; no shading, no modelling, no texture, no folds in the clothing, no patterns on fabric, no hair strands, no individual leaves or stones. Faces are simple: a few strokes for eyes, nose, mouth and beard – recognisable and expressive, but not detailed. Hands are simplified. Backgrounds are left out or reduced to one pale wash or a single line; at most one simple hint of the place. Crowds are only a few loosely suggested figures that fade into the paper. Small muted palette: sand, ochre, terracotta, blue-grey, olive, soft ink grey. Natural adult proportions. No photorealism, no anime, no glossy or cinematic light. First-century Galilee and Judea: plain garments and head coverings, sandals, earthenware, stone.
